A finite controller based on returning error trajectories
1 November 2026 (Australia/Brisbane)

Research status
===============
This investigation derives a physical-model construction, ordinary proofs, and
independent executable checks. Historical novelty, laboratory realization, and
practical superiority over the strongest conventional methods are unestablished.
The main result includes continuing sensor noise during finite meter interaction,
feedback latency, readout and reset. It allows constant classical report errors.
Protected reference memory, specified coherent interactions, and a shared static
native noise axis remain material premises. Generic quantum controller faults
are separately charged; this is not a fault-tolerance threshold theorem.

The initial scientific objective was a quantum sensor whose improving precision
does not demand equally improving knowledge of an environmental noise direction.
The strongest ordinary known-noise QEC constructions were considered first.
Their failure with a nuisance noise direction identified the opening. The useful
result changes the physical operation set by allowing scalar reservoir-rate
control. That operation is neither free information nor an ordinary Pauli pulse.

1. Task and exact physical contract
==================================
There is one sensing qubit S with unknown frequency omega and one protected
reference qubit A. Z|0>=|0>, Z|1>=-|1>. Encode a logical qubit by

    |0_L>=|0_S 0_A>,    |1_L>=|1_S 1_A>.

Its input can be unknown and entangled with an arbitrary untouched reference R.
For the final sensing task the input is |+_L>. The sensor has Hamiltonian
H_omega=omega Z_S/2 and Markov noise

    L_theta=sqrt(gamma) J_theta,
    J_theta=cos(theta) X_S+sin(theta) Y_S.

The azimuth theta is unknown, constant, and common to every native-rate setting.
Two strictly positive rates gamma_l<gamma_h can be selected. The physical control
changes only this scalar coefficient. It does not turn off the noise, resolve
theta, add an independently oriented noise source, or alter H_omega. A microscopic
resource consistent with this contract is a tunable scalar coupling to one fixed
system operator J_theta and a sufficiently broad stationary Markov reservoir.

# Finite-interval jump-count echo and accessible-bath obstruction

Independent derivation supporting the root investigation, 1 November 2026.

## Model and encoding

Sensor Hamiltonian H = omega Z/2, state-independent Hermitian Markov jump L_theta = sqrt(gamma)(cos(theta) X + sin(theta) Y). One noiseless ancilla. Code |0_L>=|00>, |1_L>=|11>. Measure ZZ parity once per fixed interval Delta and apply nominal X on the sensor iff parity is odd. Boundary measurements and corrections are ideal in the exact theorem below; their duration and error are separate physical costs.

Let J_theta = cos(theta)X + sin(theta)Y. Then J_theta^2=I and X J_theta = exp(i theta Z). During one interval a Poisson jump history with count m and jump times generates the corrected logical unitary

    U_history = exp(i theta (m mod 2) Z_L) exp(-i omega Y Z_L/2),
    Y = integral_0^Delta (-1)^(N_s) ds.

This follows by commuting all sensor Z rotations to the right through J_theta. Hidden even jump pairs cancel their theta dependence exactly. Every odd *syndrome episode*, regardless of its actual jump count, contributes exactly one theta rotation.

## Exact finite-interval instrument

Define q_o=(1-exp(-2 gamma Delta))/2 and q_e=1-q_o. Let

    d = sqrt(gamma^2-omega^2),
    F_e = exp(-gamma Delta)[cosh(d Delta) - i omega sinh(d Delta)/d],
    F_o = exp(-gamma Delta) gamma sinh(d Delta)/d,
    f_p = F_p/q_p.

At d=0 the expression is continued using sinh(d Delta)/d -> Delta. For |omega|>gamma it is interpreted by analytic continuation (sine and cosine). F_p is the characteristic function E[exp(-i omega Y) 1_{N_Delta mod 2=p}], derived from the two-state tilted generator

    [[-gamma-i omega, gamma], [gamma, -gamma+i omega]].

Conditional on syndrome p, the logical populations are unchanged and coherence rho_01 is multiplied by

    exp(i 2 p theta) f_p.

The syndrome probabilities q_p are independent of omega, theta, logical input, and any reference entanglement. Therefore this is an instrument equality on arbitrary joint logical-reference states, not only a chosen sensing input.

A sensor qubit has H = omega Z/2 and noise jump
L_theta = sqrt(gamma) A_theta, A_theta = cos(theta) X + sin(theta) Y.
gamma > 0 is known; omega and the stationary theta are unknown. The Lindblad
generator is -i[omega Z/2,rho] + gamma(A_theta rho A_theta-rho).
For each KNOWN theta, its Lindblad span is span_R{I,A_theta}; Z lies outside.
The 2018 HNLS theorem therefore permits Heisenberg time scaling with a noiseless
ancilla and arbitrarily fast accurate processing. Our question retains theta as
an unknown nuisance and charges all sensor exposure used to learn it.
